record_notes.DCP-LETT-1397: April 3, 1851. Fossil monograph printed/completed but copies not yet distributed; hopes end of month. Specimens ready for packing and return deferred to accompany copies. P2 all specimens returned describes intended contents, not completed dispatch, clarified by P3 future first packet. Refixing/reordering cards retains locality labels and explains blanks; museum duplicates requested. Declines additional recent specimens due to anticipated imminent press. Later actual copy delay to September is not yet known. No identified incoming prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1454: September 9 with supplied 1851 year. Finally obtained all memoir copies three days ago, September 6, and now packed specimens with four separately allocated copies. Steamer dispatch September 17 is future; September 12 account-book payment does not prove actual sailing or recipient receipt. Fossil volume distinct from recent volume still in proofs. Ray Society membership and later presentation-list deletion do not backdate knowledge. Earlier donor assistance is established but missing present incoming prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1459: October 16 with supplied 1851 year. New Steenstrup Xenobalanus group differs from Madeira specimens received about a year earlier. Darwin unpublished manuscript name Siphonicella acknowledged without priority; asks publication reference to correct proof. Reinhardt Danish paper received but unreadable; plate supplies understood boring mechanism. Earlier 1850 drawing witness 1330 already establishes exposure, so this retrospective first-led language is not a first October 1851 knowledge date. Returned-loan arrival merely hoped. Later synonym changes and full descriptions remain apparatus.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1461: November 4 with supplied 1851 year. Repeats unresolved Xenobalanus publication-reference request from October 16. The unanswered request is not a reply to Darwin own outgoing letter or proof a reference has arrived. Historical request retained without synthetic prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1469: January 3 with supplied 1852 year. Requests actual comparison with Spengler collection: Lepas mitra tube/colour/rib characters and large/small attached Balanus specimens versus purpurea and balanoides varieties. Explicitly permits disarticulation and destruction, a source instruction about historical specimens only. Still requests Xenobalanus publication/habitat, anticipates Ray Society volume distribution and admits specimens may not be supposed species. Questions are not prefilled with later nomenclature. Surviving Steenstrup April 8 draft specifically answers comparative request.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1478A: April 8, 1852, preserved as translation from Danish draft rather than proven verbatim final letter. P1–5 explains collection disorder after Beck retirement, prolonged search, museum permission and actual proposed box contents, with exact large/small paired-specimen comparisons and absent mitra shell despite retained labelled operculum. Identifies comparisons uncertain and revises first impressions. P6 acknowledges fossil specimens/book received and reports interest in males while waiting for recent monograph; explicitly denies demonstrated hermaphroditism. P7 independently introduces midden research, tool/bone counts, former islands and extinct fauna; retain source Iceland wording and numerical claims without geographic repair. P8 is dated recipient docket. Footnote 3 says specimens returned April 1851, contradicted by April and September Darwin letters showing delayed return; source bodies control. No evidence dates Darwin receipt of this translated draft or creates knowledge activation.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1589: September 7 with supplied 1854 year, corroborated by postmark. Offers about seventy-seven named species with varieties and localities mostly attached, to repay former fossil loans. Actual full enclosure independently read: numbered 1–77, plus two unnumbered separator rows, preserved as list items rather than table; ditto dashes and tentative variety punctuation kept. These are named species entries, not seventy-seven individual specimens. Plans to pack/send when route found; assumes acceptance because recipient busy. Ray membership explains no extra last-volume gift. Later museum holdings confirm later survival, not dispatch/receipt on September 7. Modern synonyms in thirty-seven notes stay separate.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-13814: Freshly reread incomplete Gray fragment, full separate Darwin note, bibliography and actual preserved hinge sketch. Broad conjectural 1846–54 derives only from possible barnacle interest; remains period/exact-date hold. P1 two/three umbonal teeth and P2 divided lateral teeth are Gray prose. Diagram viewed as five slanting loop/tooth marks between two horizontal boundaries, without labels or scale. Darwin separately says he looked at Arcadae series but case not good to quote; this undated layer does not inherit incoming date or establish an exact receipt. Modern taxodont explanation is editorial, not Darwin voice.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1383: Conjectural January 1851 based on Balanus completion December 30, 1850. Tomorrow at ten cannot be assigned exact day; January/February visits in account book do not identify which trip. Requests Spengler volume already shown once, remaining sessile collection and Cocks material. Editorial summary identifies a 1758 title while footnote/bibliography identify Spengler 1790; retain version conflict rather than silently claiming one source read. Completion of Balanus is current project milestone, not completion of all barnacle work. No incoming prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1564: March 28 with supplied 1854 year. Missing Grey offer to supply Erebus/Terror parts prompts list of possessed pages because numbering is nonconsecutive; list itself is not reproduced. Busk copy still sought from trustees, collection in about three weeks prospective. Requests retaining Darwin names and asks arrangement progress, while Cuming cabinet supervision is planned. Later holdings and bibliography do not establish receipt or reading of missing parts on March 28. J. E. Gray is distinct from Asa and G. R. Gray.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1155: Explicit prior primary full reading reused with matching pins. Sunday cover, February 5 or 6, likely February 6 per alteration Sa to Sunday and footnote; do not erase disjoint uncertainty. Received Gray note yesterday announcing trustee liberality. During composition changes mind and encloses thanks 1153. Not ready for specimens for about six weeks; anatomy revisits ongoing. Asks named genera/species and synonym help, has Stutchbury collection, thanks Gray representation to trustees. These are missing Gray note and report, not the later August draft. Later 1851 published synonym policy is separate. Relative receipt yesterday remains conditional on unresolved composition day.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1187: Explicit prior primary full reading reused with matching pins. June 28, supplied month/year. Promises return of Ranzani tomorrow by carrier; says little benefit, which is still evidence of consultation. Requests Conchotrya/Brisnæus now to compare with Lithotrya and optionally attached Octomeris for anatomy. Future specimen delivery and book return are not completed events. Slow monograph complaint does not identify incoming letter; 1196 concerns a later publication dispute, not this loan request.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1196: Explicit prior primary full reading reused with matching pins. August 26, 1848 autograph draft. Gray answers recent misunderstanding communicated by Darwin, recalls earlier synonym help request, explains catalogue papers intended to facilitate Darwin work and says he will withdraw unpublished papers. Postscript excepts two March papers already in type. His claims of oral credit and specimen illustrations conflict with or exceed later printed-text evidence in editorial note; preserve the historical self-report without silently correcting it. P4 recalls 1155 request, but immediate occasion is recent interview and cannot be reduced to a February-to-August reply pair. 1197 explicitly answers this reconciliation letter, though draft wording is not automatically the exact delivered text.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1197: Explicit prior primary full reading reused with matching pins. August 29, supplied 1848. Thanks Gray letter and repeats recent interview in writing. Defends Gray original suggestion and assistance to four unnamed critics, acknowledges his right to publish prior work, explains fear of losing novel species as reward for labour, confirms previous synonym request and promises to convey Gray assurances. Distinctive anticipation dispute, assurances and synonym acknowledgment identify 1196, not general barnacle topic. Oral discussion and unidentified critics are additional inputs. Future publication of acknowledgment and informing critics are intentions, not completed acts. Draft-versus-sent-text difference remains an export hold.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1317: Explicit prior primary full reading reused with matching pins. April 3, supplied 1850. Thirty-three fossil pedunculate species fully described; specimens with Sowerby for drawing, return future. Society offer to publish does not establish press commencement. Seven numbered taxonomic propositions in P2 are contemporary and later revised; preserve literal Oxunaspis and uncertain relationships rather than replacing with final nomenclature. P3 and P5 ask stratigraphic/location and valve-association questions, not established answers. Duplicate gifts requested. Spengler already consulted; northern named material still desired. Later Maastricht editorial explanation is not current knowledge.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1330: Explicit prior primary full reading reused with matching pins. Additional full reading of May 20 with supplied 1850 year, Darwin to Steenstrup. Missing reply answers questions, drawings of loan specimens delayed, northern material still anticipated. Specifically thanks Lithotrya drawing and says indicated boring manner new to him: establishes drawing known by May 20, not first seen December 25. Hermaphroditism work heard of but unseen, Danish unreadable and German difficult; later November reading/translation remain later. Keep literal improbable hermaphroditism wording distinct from editor explanation about self-fertilization. Injured Balanus and parasitic males are contemporary observations. This is another outgoing witness, not preserved incoming drawing text or a direct pair.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1342: Explicit prior primary full reading reused with matching pins. June 15, supplied 1850. Plates in engraver hands; requests additional specimens under alternative labels Anatifera cretae or Oxynaspis? or Scalpellum?, not three firmly separate species. Question marks preserve unsettled classification. No new incoming letter body survives.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1351: Explicit prior primary full reading reused with matching pins. September 1, supplied 1850. July 29 letter had been received earlier; Darwin delayed thanks until specimens arrived this morning. Two cards may have lost a shell. Return of earlier loans awaits engraving. Literal Augelin is a misreading of Angelin; preserve author text and separate editorial identification. Pedunculated manuscript finished, forty-first Balanus described, at least six months more work estimated. Lithotrya plate seen, offered paper still requested and not proved read. Named localities desired and Uddevallensis description query unanswered.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1079: Explicit prior primary reading reused with matching accepted source pins. Watson-to-Hooker third-party letter, not a target or Darwin incoming voice. Prior April 18, 1847 reading/copying witness remains unchanged. No new relationship or current-period knowledge date is created by its presence in worker additional review.
